description: Evaluation benchmarks for the WTF (Walk Through Foundations) skill, verifying visual graphs, progressive pacing, audience calibration, and active checks.

evals.name: db-index-fundamentals
assertions: Provides a 3-4 step roadmap before deep diving
Includes a visual diagram (Mermaid flowchart or ASCII tree) illustrating B-Tree search
Uses an intuitive physical analogy (e.g. alphabetized book, library catalog)
Ends Piece 1 with an active micro-check question and pauses for user response

evals.name: git-rebase-vs-merge
evals.prompt: wtf is git rebase and why do seniors love it so much?
assertions: Outlines a concise piece-by-piece learning roadmap
Includes a git branch/commit graph showing replay of commits onto a new base
Clarifies that commit SHAs change during rebase
Concludes the first piece with a thought experiment regarding public branches

evals.name: kafka-streaming-eli5
evals.prompt: wtf is Apache Kafka explain like I am 10
assertions: Uses child-accessible physical metaphor (conveyor belt, notebook, post office)
Zero impenetrable jargon (no unexplained zookeeper/kraft/broker terminology)
Includes a clear visual diagram showing producer -> log -> consumer
Presents an active check checking understanding of the conveyor belt

evals.name: event-loop-javascript
evals.prompt: /wtf is the JavaScript event loop? why doesn't setTimeout(fn, 0) run immediately?
assertions: Breaks down Call Stack, Web APIs, and Task Queue in a clear roadmap
Features a visual sequence or flow diagram showing queue ordering
Explains the 0ms delay mechanism intuitively
Tests mental model with a predict-the-console-output micro-puzzle

evals.name: k8s-vs-serverless-executive
evals.prompt: wtf is Kubernetes and why is my team asking for a $200k migration from Lambda? explain like I am VP of Product
assertions: Calibrates tone to executive altitude focusing on total cost of ownership, blast radius, and team velocity
Avoids low-level container internals (cgroups, kubelet, etcd) in favor of operational tradeoffs
Includes a clear visual comparison diagram (Mermaid quadrant or tradeoff chart)
Concludes Piece 1 with an active check on operational workload characteristics

evals.name: python-gil-multithreading
evals.prompt: wtf is Python GIL? I added 8 threads to my CPU-bound loop and it ran SLOWER than 1 thread?!
assertions: Outlines a clear roadmap distinguishing CPU-bound vs I/O-bound threading
Includes a visual diagram (Mermaid state/timeline or ASCII) showing thread contention and mutex lock bouncing
Explains the OS context-switching overhead and cache trashing mechanism clearly
Ends Piece 1 with an active check on whether multiprocessing vs multithreading applies

evals.name: raft-consensus-split-brain
evals.prompt: wtf is Raft consensus and how does it prevent split-brain during network partition?
assertions: Presents a rigorous 3-4 piece roadmap covering leader election, term numbers, and log replication
Includes a visual network topology diagram (Mermaid) showing 3 vs 2 node partition and majority quorum
Explains the mathematical quorum rule (N/2 + 1) without hand-waving
Ends Piece 1 with an active check on partition voting behavior

evals.name: cpu-cache-lines-false-sharing
evals.prompt: wtf is CPU false sharing and why did my multi-threaded struct benchmark tank?
assertions: Roadmap breaks down L1/L2 cache lines, MESI cache coherency, and cache bouncing
Includes a visual memory layout diagram (ASCII or Mermaid) showing 64-byte cache line alignment
Explains why adjacent memory writes invalidate neighbor cores' caches
Ends Piece 1 with an active puzzle on struct padding or memory alignment
